script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for September 11. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Leaves fall.  Animals die.  Yet forests aren't buried in corpses.

Decomposers don't destroy—they recycle. The nitrogen in a fallen leaf becomes the nitrogen in a growing sprout. Matter cycles endlessly; decomposers are the recycling centers. Decomposers work invisibly underground or in decay.  They're not glamorous, but they're essential.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Endings enable beginnings.  Breakdown creates raw material for new growth.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Decomposition Practice - Convert an Ending.

Here's your activity: What has recently ended—a project, relationship, phase of life? What 'nutrients' can you extract? Lessons, skills, connections? Consciously decompose endings into raw materials for what's next. This helps you transform endings into new raw materials.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about nature's cleanup crew can be applied to decomposition practice - convert an ending. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
